category_title: Year 9 boys with SEBD who resist modified games and technical practice
minimal_context: The student is participating in a Year 9 Physical Education class where the goal is to complete a peer assessment task identifying a partner's strengths and weaknesses.
dialogue:
TUTOR: For this next activity, I need you to work with your partner and identify their personal strengths and weaknesses from the game.

STUDENT: (Wanders away from his partner) I'm not doing this paired stuff.

TUTOR: Please go back to your partner and try the assessment.

STUDENT: (Walks back over) Fine. Your weakness is that you're completely useless at passing.

TUTOR: What do you think would be a better way to say that?

STUDENT: No, it's true, he's an idiot! (Starts arguing aggressively with the partner) You can't even kick the ball straight, you're terrible!

options.A: Implement a daily point system, with his daily goal set at him making 80% of the possible points each day.
options.B: Physically mark the field into three zones and focus instruction on passing to the 'danger zones' (front and back thirds).
options.C: Change the game playing routine by taking names out of a hat at random to nominate partners for the peer assessment.
options.D: Implement a systematic learning approach that encourages exploration and social interaction during physical education activities.
